title: Something new under the Sun: A magnetically driven CH/CN anti-correlation
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures. A&A, in press. Abstract shortened for arXiv
summary: Spectroscopic monitoring surveys have shown that the magnetic cycle alters the photospheric structure of the Sun, perturbing the formation of molecular lines. In parallel, the study of Globular Clusters has remained centred on the multiple stellar populations conundrum, a phenomenon defined-most notably-by the anti-correlation between CH and CN molecular bands, serving to distinguish between first-population and second-population stars. We systematically monitored the behaviour of the CH and CN molecular bands as a function of the solar magnetic cycle. We demonstrate that the disc-integrated solar spectrum exhibits a distinct CH/CN anti-correlation driven by the magnetic cycle. Our results suggest that the spectroscopic and photometric anomalies defining the multiple populations conundrum may be physically linked to a differential spectral response to varying degrees of surface magnetic coverage.

AI.tldr: The Sun's disc-integrated spectrum shows a CH/CN anti-correlation driven by the solar magnetic cycle, analogous to the CH-CN anti-correlation used to distinguish stellar populations in Globular Clusters. This suggests that the spectroscopic anomalies defining the multiple populations conundrum may be physically linked to differential spectral responses to varying surface magnetic coverage.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the CH/CN anti-correlation observed in Globular Cluster stellar populations has a physical origin related to magnetic activity, by studying the Sun as a benchmark where magnetic cycle effects can be directly monitored.
AI.method: Systematic spectroscopic monitoring of the CH and CN molecular band strengths in the disc-integrated solar spectrum as a function of the solar magnetic cycle.
AI.result: The disc-integrated solar spectrum exhibits a distinct CH/CN anti-correlation modulated by the magnetic cycle, demonstrating that magnetic activity alone can produce this molecular band anti-correlation.
AI.conclusion: The CH/CN anti-correlation defining multiple stellar populations in Globular Clusters may not require distinct chemical compositions; instead, it could be a differential spectral response to varying degrees of surface magnetic coverage.

title: The Bimodal Mass Ratio Distribution of the Hyades
summary: The distribution of stellar mass ratios, q, in binary systems provides critical insights into the dynamical history and star-formation processes of open clusters. Here, I re-evaluate the recently published mass ratio distribution (MRD) of a sample of spectroscopic binaries in the Hyades cluster, which was based on stellar positions in colour-magnitude diagrams. I demonstrate that the mass ratios derived in that work are statistically inconsistent with a random distribution of orbital inclinations. Furthermore, several systems yielded non-physical results. By applying a Richardson-Lucy deconvolution to the spectroscopic mass functions and assuming a random distribution of inclinations, I re-derive the MRD for this sample, showing that it is statistically different from a uniform distribution. I further find a significant dependence on the primary mass: systems with lower-mass primaries exhibit a peak near q~1, whereas more massive primaries show a distribution heavily skewed toward low mass ratios (q~0.15). These findings highlight the potential pitfalls of photometric mass ratio derivations and underscore the need for further verification with future data releases such as Gaia DR4.

AI.tldr: This paper re-evaluates the mass ratio distribution (MRD) of spectroscopic binaries in the Hyades cluster, finding that previously derived mass ratios based on colour-magnitude diagrams are statistically inconsistent with a random inclination distribution and include non-physical results. Using Richardson-Lucy deconvolution on spectroscopic mass functions, the author derives a new MRD that differs from uniform, revealing a primary-mass dependence: low-mass primaries peak near q~1 while massive primaries skew toward q~0.15.
AI.motivation: To critically assess the recently published MRD of spectroscopic binaries in the Hyades cluster, as photometric mass ratio derivations may be unreliable, and to obtain a more physically consistent MRD using proper statistical methods.
AI.method: The author tests the previously published MRD against a random orbital inclination assumption, identifies inconsistencies and non-physical results, then applies a Richardson-Lucy deconvolution technique to the spectroscopic mass functions assuming random inclinations to re-derive the MRD.
AI.result: The re-derived MRD is statistically different from a uniform distribution and exhibits a strong primary-mass dependence: lower-mass primaries show a peak near q~1, while more massive primaries display a distribution heavily skewed toward low mass ratios (q~0.15).
AI.conclusion: Photometric mass ratio derivations can be highly unreliable, and further verification is needed with future data releases such as Gaia DR4.

title: New Spatially Resolved Observations of Betelgeuse from the VLA and ALMA: Evidence for Atmospheric Perturbations from a Close Companion
comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the Astronomical Journal
summary: We present new spatially resolved observations of the red supergiant Betelgeuse ($α$ Orionis) at seven frequencies: 22 GHz ($λ$1.36cm); 44 GHz ($λ$6.8mm); 107 GHz ($λ$2.8mm); 136 GHz ($λ$2.2mm); 224 GHz ($λ$1.3mm); 338 GHz ($λ$0.89mm); and 485 GHz ($λ$0.62mm) using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. These observations (spanning 2021-2026) enable a characterization of the mean brightness temperature ($T_B$), shape, and symmetry of the star's extended atmosphere. At 22 GHz and 44 GHz $T_B$ has increased following the historic lows observed in 2019, just prior to the Great Dimming of late 2019/early 2020. We find that $T_B$ peaks at a larger projected radius ($r\sim2.7R_{\star}$) compared with measurements prior to 2016, consistent with a possible evolution in the atmospheric density profile. In addition we find a systematic decrease in $T_B$ from $\approx3500$K at $\sim2.7R_{\star}$ to $T_{B}\approx$2220K at $\sim1.2R_{\star}$, confirming a previously reported temperature minimum between the photosphere and chromosphere. At all observed frequencies $T_B$ is lower than temperatures inferred from ultraviolet measurements at comparable radii, indicating the continued presence of cooler plasma ($T\le T_{\rm eff}$) mixed with the warmer chromospheric material. The new measurements yield a global spectral index $α=1.35\pm$0.03, with no evidence for a change in $α$ over more than two decades in frequency. Recently, evidence of a close-in companion to Betelgeuse has been reported, with an orbital separation $r\sim2.3R_{\star}$. We have identified a correlation between the ellipticity of Betelgeuse, as obtained from radio measurements, and the companion's orbital phase. The results are consistent with periodic perturbations of the atmosphere by the companion.

AI.tldr: New spatially resolved radio observations of Betelgeuse at seven frequencies (22-485 GHz) spanning 2021-2026 reveal that mean brightness temperature has increased since 2019 lows and peaks at larger projected radius than pre-2016, confirming a temperature minimum between photosphere and chromosphere. The data show a global spectral index of α=1.35±0.03, and an ellipticity correlated with a reported companion's orbital phase suggests atmospheric perturbation by a close-in companion at r~2.3R★.
AI.motivation: To characterize the extended atmosphere of Betelgeuse (a red supergiant) across multiple radio frequencies after its Great Dimming event in 2019/2020, to track recovery of brightness temperature, probe the atmospheric density/temperature structure, and investigate evidence for a close-in companion perturbing the stellar atmosphere.
AI.method: Spatially resolved radio interferometric observations using the Karl G. Jansky VLA and ALMA at seven frequencies (22, 44, 107, 136, 224, 338, 485 GHz). Mean brightness temperature, shape, and symmetry were characterized, and the global spectral index was derived. Correlations between measured radio ellipticity and the companion's orbital phase were examined.
AI.result: T_B increased at 22 and 44 GHz following 2019 lows; T_B peaks at r~2.7R★ (larger than pre-2016) and decreases from ~3500K at 2.7R★ to ~2220K at 1.2R★. T_B is systematically lower than UV-inferred temperatures, indicating cool plasma mixed with warm chromospheric material. Spectral index α=1.35±0.03 shows no change over two decades in frequency. Radio ellipticity correlates with the companion's orbital phase.
AI.conclusion: Betelgeuse's atmosphere has evolved since the Great Dimming, with a peak in T_B at larger radius than before and a persistent temperature minimum between photosphere and chromosphere. The correlation between radio ellipticity and companion orbital phase supports the hypothesis that a close-in companion periodically perturbs Betelgeuse's extended atmosphere.

title: Visual Orbits of Spectroscopic Binaries with the CHARA Array. V. HD 210763 and HD 221950
summary: We present the visual orbits and dynamical masses of two longer period spectroscopic binary stars, HD 210763 and HD 221950, using long baseline interferometry with the CHARA Array and high resolution spectroscopy with the APO 3.5 m and CTIO 1.5 m telescopes. By combining the astrometric and radial velocity observations, we solve for the full, three-dimensional orbits and determine the stellar masses to within 0.5% uncertainty and the distance to within 0.2% uncertainty. For HD 210763, we found component masses of M1 = 1.748 Msun and M2 = 1.492 Msun. For HD 221950, we found masses of M1 = 1.098 Msun and M2 = 1.031 Msun. We then estimate the effective temperature and radius of each component star through disentangling and spectral energy distribution analyses. We compare the observed stellar parameters to the predictions of the stellar evolution models and estimate the system ages. The primary component of HD 210763 is at the end of the main sequence while the secondary component is on the main sequence, providing a tight age constraint for this system at 1.6 Gyr. Both components of HD 221950 are still on the main sequence with an age of 3.76 Gyr. These systems have longer orbital periods, beyond the tidal circularization limit, and therefore are better proxies for single stars and tests of stellar evolution models than short period, eclipsing systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents visual orbits and dynamical masses for two long-period spectroscopic binary systems (HD 210763 and HD 221950) determined using CHARA Array interferometry and high-resolution spectroscopy. Combined astrometric and radial velocity data yield masses to within 0.5% uncertainty and distances to within 0.2%. The systems serve as better proxies for single stars than short-period eclipsing binaries, as their longer orbital periods lie beyond the tidal circularization limit.
AI.motivation: To obtain high-precision dynamical masses and stellar parameters for longer-period binary systems, which are better tests of stellar evolution models than short-period eclipsing systems because they avoid complications from tidal circularization and are more representative of isolated single stars.
AI.method: The study combines long-baseline interferometry with the CHARA Array (for visual astrometric orbits) and high-resolution spectroscopy from APO 3.5 m and CTIO 1.5 m telescopes (for radial velocities). These data were jointly fit to derive full three-dimensional orbits, dynamical masses, and distances. Effective temperatures and radii were estimated via spectral disentangling and spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis, followed by comparison to stellar evolution model predictions.
AI.result: For HD 210763: M1 = 1.748 Msun, M2 = 1.492 Msun, system age ~1.6 Gyr with primary near end of main sequence and secondary on main sequence. For HD 221950: M1 = 1.098 Msun, M2 = 1.031 Msun, system age ~3.76 Gyr with both components on the main sequence. Masses determined to within 0.5% and distances to within 0.2% uncertainty.
AI.conclusion: These long-period binaries provide stringent tests of stellar evolution models with high-precision dynamical masses. Their beyond-tidal-circularization orbital periods make them superior proxies for single stars compared to short-period eclipsing binaries, enabling tight age constraints at 1.6 Gyr and 3.76 Gyr for the two systems.

title: Lithium as a Signpost for Compact Object Binary Candidates in the LAMOST Medium Resolution Survey
comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, to be published in Research Notes of the AAS
summary: Binary systems with black hole or neutron star companions are often associated with lithium enhancement. Gaia NS1, a recently discovered neutron-star binary with a lithium-enhanced main-sequence companion, demonstrates the potential of lithium as a signpost for identifying compact object binaries in existing spectroscopic surveys. In particular, we aim to use lithium as a signpost to find compact object binaries similar to Gaia NS1 in the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fibre Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) Medium Resolution Survey (MRS). From LAMOST MRS, we selected 4441 metal-poor main-sequence stars like Gaia NS1, measured the Li 6707 Å equivalent width, and then identified a sample of 33 stars with strong Li absorption. We used radial velocity variation and astrometric binarity signatures from Gaia, narrowing the sample to 3 candidates. We identified one of these candidates as an eclipsing binary and demonstrated that massive companions for the other two are unlikely via follow-up spectroscopy.

AI.tldr: The paper uses lithium (Li 6707 Å) as a chemical signpost to find compact object binaries similar to Gaia NS1 in the LAMOST Medium Resolution Survey, narrowing 4441 metal-poor main-sequence stars down to 33 Li-strong stars, then 3 candidates via radial velocity and astrometric binary signatures, ultimately finding one eclipsing binary and ruling out massive companions for the other two.
AI.motivation: Binary systems containing black holes or neutron stars are often associated with lithium enhancement, and the recent discovery of Gaia NS1 (a neutron-star binary with a lithium-enhanced companion) suggests lithium could serve as a powerful signpost to identify compact object binaries in existing spectroscopic surveys.
AI.method: The authors selected 4441 metal-poor main-sequence stars similar to Gaia NS1 from LAMOST MRS, measured their Li 6707 Å equivalent widths, selected 33 stars with strong Li absorption, then applied radial velocity variation and Gaia astrometric binarity signatures to narrow the sample to 3 candidates, followed by follow-up spectroscopy.
AI.result: From the 3 candidates identified, one was confirmed as an eclipsing binary, while follow-up spectroscopy demonstrated that the other two are unlikely to host massive (compact object) companions.
AI.conclusion: Lithium serves as an effective chemical signpost for identifying compact object binary candidates in large spectroscopic surveys, although follow-up observations are essential to confirm or rule out the presence of massive compact companions.

title: Investigating Possible Stellar Coronal Mass Ejections in M-type Dwarfs Using the CARMENES DR1 Spectra
summary: Stellar coronal mass ejections (CMEs) have significant impacts on surrounding exoplanets and stellar evolution. For M-type dwarf stars, hosting close-in habitable zones, frequent and intense stellar CMEs may render their potentially habitable planets uninhabitable. In this study, we used the CARMENES DR1 spectra to investigate potential stellar CMEs in M-type dwarfs by analyzing asymmetric features of the Hα profiles. Through a comprehensive visual inspection, we identified 61 distinct asymmetric features in the Hα line profiles across 33 M-type dwarfs. These asymmetries were associated with increased emissions in several chromospheric activity lines, indicating likely connections to flare events. The velocities of these features remain below the escape velocities of the investigated stars, except for one case where an asymmetric feature's maximum velocity approaches the star's escape velocity. While stellar CMEs are one potential explanation, the observed features are also consistent with other flare-related plasma motions. The estimated moving plasma masses range from 10^15 to 10^19 g, with corresponding kinetic energies of 10^29--10^32 erg. Stars with asymmetric Hα profiles are generally associated with stronger surface-average magnetic field <B> and higher normalized X-ray luminosity log(L_X/L_bol). However, we find no significant correlation between the line asymmetry rate and either <B> or log(L_X/L_bol).

AI.tldr: Using CARMENES DR1 spectra, the authors identified 61 distinct asymmetric Hα line features across 33 M-type dwarfs, suggesting potential stellar coronal mass ejections (CMEs). The features are associated with increased chromospheric emission and flare activity, with plasma masses of 10^15-10^19 g and kinetic energies of 10^29-10^32 erg. Most feature velocities remain below the stars' escape velocities, and no significant correlation was found between line asymmetry rate and magnetic field or X-ray luminosity.
AI.motivation: Stellar CMEs from M-type dwarf stars can significantly impact the habitability of close-in exoplanets. Understanding the frequency and properties of these CMEs is crucial for assessing whether potentially habitable planets around M dwarfs can retain their atmospheres and remain habitable.
AI.method: The study analyzed CARMENES DR1 spectra of M-type dwarfs, performing a comprehensive visual inspection of Hα line profiles to identify asymmetric features indicative of CMEs. The features were cross-referenced with chromospheric activity line emissions, and their velocities were compared to stellar escape velocities. Plasma masses and kinetic energies were estimated, and correlations with surface-average magnetic field strength and X-ray luminosity were examined.
AI.result: 61 asymmetric Hα features were found across 33 M-type dwarfs, linked to flare-related activity. Most feature velocities are below escape velocity (one exception approaching it). Estimated plasma masses range 10^15-10^19 g with kinetic energies of 10^29-10^32 erg. Stars with asymmetric Hα profiles show stronger magnetic fields and higher normalized X-ray luminosities, but no significant correlation was found between the line asymmetry rate and either of these parameters.
AI.conclusion: Stellar CMEs are a plausible explanation for the observed asymmetric Hα features in M-type dwarfs, although other flare-related plasma motions remain consistent with the data. These events could have significant implications for exoplanet habitability around M dwarfs, but the lack of correlation between CME occurrence rate and magnetic/X-ray activity suggests that predicting CME activity from these parameters alone may not be straightforward.

title: A Possible Stellar CME Event Associated with a Long-duration Optical Flare on the RS CVn-type Star UX Arietis
summary: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are large-scale eruptions of magnetized plasma from stellar coronae, and they are always accompanied by flares. In this study, we present high-resolution spectroscopic observations of a long-duration optical flare on the RS CVn-type star UX Arietis (UX Ari). Around the flare peak, we have detected a far-blueshifted emission component in the H$α$ line profile---a signature of an erupting prominence---indicating a possible stellar CME. After correcting for projection effects, the eruption velocity reaches $\sim -432$ km s$^{-1}$ when assuming radial propagation, significantly exceeding the escape velocity of the primary component ($\approx 304$ km s$^{-1}$). This strongly supports the detection of a stellar CME. The mass of this CME is at least $2.7 \times 10^{20}$ g, and its kinetic energy is $2.5 \times 10^{35}$ erg. The mass value is consistent with the solar flare--CME scaling relation, while its kinetic energy lies below the solar trend. The flare itself released an energy of $4.2 \times 10^{36}$ erg in the H$α$, corresponding to a white-light bolometric energy of roughly $2.8 \times 10^{38}$ erg. Throughout the flaring event, evolving asymmetries in the H$α$ profile reveal complex plasma dynamics.

AI.tldr: High-resolution Hα spectroscopic observations of a long-duration optical flare on the RS CVn-type star UX Arietis reveal a far-blueshifted emission component near flare peak, interpreted as a stellar coronal mass ejection (CME) with an eruption velocity of ~432 km s⁻¹ (exceeding the escape velocity of ~304 km s⁻¹), a mass of ≥2.7×10²⁰ g, and kinetic energy of 2.5×10³⁵ erg. The CME mass aligns with the solar flare–CME scaling relation, though its kinetic energy falls below the solar trend. The flare released 4.2×10³⁶ erg in Hα, corresponding to ~2.8×10³⁸ erg in white-light bolometric energy.
AI.motivation: To detect and characterize stellar coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from active stars using high-resolution spectroscopic observations, which is crucial for understanding stellar magnetic activity, mass loss, and the flare–CME relationship beyond our Sun.
AI.method: High-resolution spectroscopic monitoring of the Hα line during a long-duration optical flare on UX Ari; measurement of the blueshifted emission component, correction of projection effects, and estimation of CME velocity, mass, and kinetic energy using the escape velocity threshold and solar scaling relations.
AI.result: Detection of a stellar CME with eruption velocity ~-432 km s⁻¹ (exceeding the ~304 km s⁻¹ escape velocity), CME mass ≥2.7×10²⁰ g, kinetic energy 2.5×10³⁵ erg, and flare energy of 4.2×10³⁶ erg in Hα (~2.8×10³⁸ erg bolometric). CME mass is consistent with the solar flare–CME scaling relation, but its kinetic energy is below the solar trend.
AI.conclusion: The observations provide strong evidence for a stellar CME on UX Ari, supporting the existence of eruptive phenomena on active stars analogous to solar CMEs. While the CME mass follows the solar scaling relation, the lower-than-solar kinetic energy suggests possible differences in flare–CME energy partitioning between the Sun and more active stars.

title: Electron transport in a radiation-dominated plasma Application to solar corona brightenings
summary: Bremsstrahlung scattering of fast electrons on ions can be enhanced by the microwave radiation present in the solar corona. It can account for the electron diffusive transport along magnetic loops and high precipitation rates. This process can also dominate the transport of thermal electrons confined in such loops. The influence of stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering on the electron transport is studied, with focus on the return current induced by the fast electron population trapped in magnetic loops. Overall, transport coefficients are reevaluated in the radiation-dominated plasma, characterized by the stimulated action of radiation on the Bremsstrahlung electron-ion collision, down to thermal velocities. We develop a theoretical framework for electron transport driven by a large bandwidth, bright low-frequency part of the photon spectrum and compute a set of radiation-enhanced transport coefficients. UV, XEUV and hard X-ray signals from flares, evidencing anomalous resistivity, thermal conduction inhibition and high precipitation rates of fast electrons, are reinterpreted. The anomalous resistivity due to stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to dominate the classical resistivity in flares. The runaway effect due to Coulomb collisions is suppressed. Thermal conduction is inhibited compared to the Spitzer conduction, in agreement with coronal seismology of slow-mode waves. Stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to be a key collisional process in flaring events. It can explain the above loop-top hard X-ray signal due to the fast electrons, and the measured electrical conductivity due to the thermal electrons. As a perspective, the corresponding transport coefficients can be used in radiation MHD codes. The radiation model could also be applied to stimulate large-angle electron scattering in the kinetic or hybrid models used to study the solar corona.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering of fast electrons on ions, enhanced by microwave radiation in the solar corona, governs electron transport in flaring magnetic loops. It develops a theoretical framework for radiation-enhanced transport coefficients and shows this process dominates classical resistivity, suppresses the Coulomb runaway effect, and inhibits thermal conduction—consistent with observations of loop-top hard X-ray emission and coronal seismology. The coefficients are suitable for radiation MHD and kinetic/hybrid coronal models.
AI.motivation: Classical Coulomb collision-based transport theories cannot fully explain observed solar flare phenomena such as anomalous resistivity, inhibited thermal conduction, and high fast-electron precipitation rates. The authors seek a physical mechanism—stimulated Bremsstrahlung in a radiation-dominated plasma—that can reconcile these observations.
AI.method: A theoretical framework is developed for electron transport driven by a broad-band, bright low-frequency photon spectrum in the solar corona. Transport coefficients are derived by including stimulated Bremsstrahlung electron-ion collisions down to thermal velocities, and the framework is applied to compute radiation-enhanced transport coefficients and to reinterpret flare observations (UV/XEUV/hard X-ray signals, resistivity, thermal conduction).
AI.result: The anomalous resistivity from stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering dominates classical resistivity in flares; the Coulomb runaway effect is suppressed; thermal conduction is inhibited relative to Spitzer conduction in agreement with slow-mode wave seismology; and the mechanism can explain loop-top hard X-ray signals from fast electrons and the measured electrical conductivity.
AI.conclusion: Stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is a key collisional process in flaring events. The derived transport coefficients can be incorporated into radiation MHD codes, and the radiation model can be extended to stimulate large-angle electron scattering in kinetic or hybrid coronal simulations.

title: The double white dwarf merger model for the progenitors of SN 2021yfj-like events
summary: Context. Recently, a new class of supernovae with prominent narrow emission features of Si, S and Ar has been reported, i.e. SN 2021yfj-like events (SNe Ien). Their progenitor origin is still unknown. It has been suggested that a massive CO WD may evolve into a Si/S-rich WD when accreting He-rich matter at a high mass-transfer rate. If the He companion subsequently evolves into another more massive WD, the merger of this double WD system can generate Si/S-rich CSM through tidal stripping. Following the SN explosion, the interaction between the SN ejecta and the Si/S-rich CSM could produce the Si, S, and Ar emission lines characteristic of SN 2021yfj-like events. Aims. In this work, we aim to determine the initial parameter space of WD+He star systems that can lead to SN 2021yfj-like events via the double WD merger scenario, and to quantify their theoretical Galactic birthrate and delay-time distributions. Methods. We perform detailed binary evolution simulations of a large number of semidetached WD+He star systems to obtain the parameter space that leads to the formation of Si/S-rich WDs and subsequent double WD mergers. We then use binary population synthesis to calculate the Galactic birthrate and delay-time distribution of such events. Results. For the formation of SN 2021yfj-like events, we found that the initial CO WD and He companion masses must lie in the ranges of 1.0-1.2 M_sun and 2.2-2.5 M_sun, respectively. The derived merger rate for this scenario is ~(2.6-4.4)x10^-5 yr^-1 with delay times longer than 450 Myr, which is about 1% of the observed SN Ia rate. Conclusions. We suggest that the double WD merger scenario involving a Si/S-rich WD originating from a CO WD+He star system, represents a significant and competitive model for SN 2021yfj-like events, underscoring the need for further observations of similar events coupled with relevant theoretical investigations.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the progenitor origin of SN 2021yfj-like supernovae (SNe Ien) through a double white dwarf merger scenario. Using binary evolution simulations and population synthesis, the authors find that initial CO WD masses of 1.0-1.2 M_sun paired with He companions of 2.2-2.5 M_sun can produce Si/S-rich WDs that merge to generate the observed emission features. The resulting Galactic birthrate is ~(2.6-4.4)x10^-5 yr^-1 with delay times >450 Myr, about 1% of the SN Ia rate, making this a competitive formation channel.
AI.motivation: The progenitor origin of the newly discovered class of supernovae with prominent narrow Si, S, and Ar emission lines (SN 2021yfj-like events, SNe Ien) is unknown. The authors aim to test and constrain the double WD merger scenario as a viable formation pathway for these events.
AI.method: The authors perform detailed binary evolution simulations of a large set of semidetached WD+He star systems to map the initial parameter space leading to the formation of Si/S-rich WDs (via high mass-transfer rate He accretion onto massive CO WDs) and subsequent double WD mergers. They then use binary population synthesis to compute the Galactic birthrate and delay-time distribution of SN 2021yfj-like events.
AI.result: The required initial masses are 1.0-1.2 M_sun for the CO WD and 2.2-2.5 M_sun for the He companion. The derived merger rate is ~(2.6-4.4)x10^-5 yr^-1 with delay times exceeding 450 Myr, corresponding to roughly 1% of the observed SN Ia rate.
AI.conclusion: The double WD merger scenario involving a Si/S-rich WD originating from a CO WD+He star system is a significant and competitive model for SN 2021yfj-like events, and further observations and theoretical work are needed to strengthen this interpretation.

title: Unravelling Mass Transfer in Algols from Surface Abundances. I. Z Vulpeculae
summary: The photospheric abundance pattern of the components is a sensitive probe of mass and angular momentum transfer in Algols. With the aim to trace the evolutionary history and disclosed efficiency of mass transfer in Algols we collected new high-resolution spectra for about a dozen Algols with the {\sc hermes} spectrograph at the Mercator Telescope on La Palma, Canary Islands. In the present paper, which is the first in the series, we present the results of a comprehensive analysis of Z Vul, a hot Algol-type system. We derived the absolute stellar quantities and elemental abundances for the components. The carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio is the most sensitive tracer of thermonuclear processing and mass transfer. It is found to be within expected value for gainer but donor lacks the severe C/N inversion traditionally expected for a deeply stripped star. An extensive grid of over three million evolutionary models was calculated with the Cambridge \texttt{STARS} code which allows determination of the best-fitting and all surviving models. Constraints from the He and CNO abundances indicate that Z Vul underwent an episode of nearly conservative mass transfer during the Main Sequence life-time of the originally more massive component (Case A). Our detailed chemical tagging confirms that the surface abundances of the mass-losing component represent the delicately stripped outer layers still not reaching the CNO-rich core. This underscores the need of coupling high-resolution spectroscopic abundances with interior stellar profiles to accurately reconstruct the evolutionary history of interacting binaries.

AI.tldr: This first paper in a series analyzes Z Vul, a hot Algol-type binary system, using high-resolution HERMES spectra to derive absolute stellar quantities and elemental abundances. The C/N ratio indicates the donor star lacks the severe C/N inversion expected for a deeply stripped star. An evolutionary grid of over three million models constrains Z Vul to have undergone nearly conservative mass transfer (Case A). The analysis confirms that donor surface abundances trace finely stripped outer layers, not yet exposing the CNO-rich core.
AI.motivation: To trace the evolutionary history and quantify the efficiency of mass transfer in Algol-type binaries by using photospheric abundance patterns as sensitive probes of mass and angular momentum transfer.
AI.method: High-resolution HERMES spectra were collected for ~12 Algols. For Z Vul, absolute stellar quantities and elemental abundances were derived from the spectra. An extensive grid of over three million evolutionary models was computed with the Cambridge STARS code to identify best-fitting and all surviving models, constrained particularly by He and CNO abundances.
AI.result: The C/N ratio of Z Vul falls within the expected range for the gainer, but the donor lacks the severe C/N inversion typically expected for a deeply stripped star. Evolutionary modeling indicates Z Vul experienced nearly conservative mass transfer during the Main Sequence lifetime of the originally more massive component (Case A).
AI.conclusion: Surface abundances of the mass-losing component in Z Vul represent delicately stripped outer layers that do not yet reach the CNO-rich core. Coupling high-resolution spectroscopic abundances with interior stellar profiles is essential for accurately reconstructing the evolutionary history of interacting binaries.

title: The symphony of pulsations and binarity among massive stars using HERMES spectroscopy and TESS photometry
comment: 24 pages, including 7 of appendices, 15 figures, 2 tables
summary: A wide range of variability mechanisms exist among intermediate mass and massive stars, which are not yet fully understood. Using complementary data sources for a large population of B- and O-type stars, we aim to study the prevalence and interplay of different types of variability, including binarity, pulsation, and rotation, to prepare for future modelling. To this end, we analyse high-resolution HERMES spectra and 2-min cadence TESS photometry and characterise the diverse variability observed within a population of 873 O- and B-type stars. The spectroscopic data were normalised using machine-learning techniques, compared to a grid of synthetic TLUSTY spectra to determine stellar parameters, and used to identify radial velocity variability. Photometric time series were analysed using standard frequency analysis methods to detect pulsations and rotational modulation signatures. We find that more than 93 per cent of the sample exhibits photometric variability. Photometric variability caused by pulsations is identified in 82 per cent of the sample, with dominant contributions from $β$ Cep and slowly pulsating B-type stars, as well as stochastic low-frequency variability. Based on a limited number of spectroscopic epochs, at least 14 per cent of the stars show evidence of binarity, including both eclipsing and spectroscopic systems. This work represents one of the largest homogeneous surveys of variability for intermediate-mass and massive stars in the Northern hemisphere, and complementing similar efforts in the Southern hemisphere. It provides a statistical framework for future studies of stellar structure and evolution, particularly in the context of asteroseismology.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes 873 O- and B-type stars using HERMES spectra and TESS photometry to characterize variability, finding that over 93% show photometric variability (82% from pulsations, including β Cep and slowly pulsating B stars), at least 14% show evidence of binarity, and the work provides one of the largest homogeneous variability surveys of intermediate-mass and massive stars in the Northern hemisphere.
AI.motivation: The variability mechanisms among intermediate mass and massive stars are not yet fully understood. The authors aim to study the prevalence and interplay of different variability types (binarity, pulsation, rotation) in a large B- and O-type star population to prepare for future modelling.
AI.method: High-resolution HERMES spectra were normalized using machine-learning techniques and compared to a grid of synthetic TLUSTY spectra to determine stellar parameters and identify radial velocity variability. TESS photometry at 2-min cadence was analyzed using standard frequency analysis methods to detect pulsations and rotational modulation signatures across 873 O- and B-type stars.
AI.result: More than 93% of the sample exhibits photometric variability. Pulsations are identified in 82% of the sample, with dominant contributions from β Cep and slowly pulsating B-type stars, plus stochastic low-frequency variability. At least 14% of stars show evidence of binarity, including both eclipsing and spectroscopic systems.
AI.conclusion: This work represents one of the largest homogeneous variability surveys for intermediate-mass and massive stars in the Northern hemisphere, complementing Southern hemisphere efforts. It provides a statistical framework for future studies of stellar structure and evolution, particularly in asteroseismology.

title: Wave excitation by a collapsing granule: insights from IFU observations and high-resolution RMHD simulations
summary:
Context. Granular collapse is an ubiquitous process of granular evolution on the solar surface, but it is hard to analyze in sufficient spatial, temporal, and spectral detail.
  Aims. We analyze the change in physical conditions in the photosphere during a specific granular collapse event and the subsequent atmospheric response.
  Methods. We contrast a high-resolution radiative magneto-hydrodynamic simulation of a granular collapse performed using the CO5BOLD code with the recent integral field unit observations carried out using the MiHI instrument at the Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope.
  Results. Our analysis shows that the observed and simulated granular collapse show remarkable similarity. Specifically, they both exhibit the signature of a wave pulse excited in the deep photosphere and visible up to the temperature minimum. This wave is detectable through a blue-wing emission in the observed and synthetic Na i D1 line. We also estimate the acoustic energy flux carried by the wave and analyze its initiation.
  Conclusions. Combining high-resolution IFU spectropolarimetry and state-of-the-art simulations of the solar lower atmosphere, this study showcases our current capabilities in identifying specific physical processes taking place during the granular collapse and their impact on the atmosphere above.

AI.tldr: This study compares a high-resolution radiative magneto-hydrodynamic simulation of a granular collapse (using CO5BOLD) with MiHI/1-m SST integral field unit observations. Both show remarkable agreement, revealing a wave pulse excited in the deep photosphere and visible up to the temperature minimum, detected via blue-wing emission in the Na i D1 line. The acoustic energy flux of this wave is estimated and its initiation analyzed.
AI.motivation: Granular collapse is a ubiquitous but poorly resolved process of granular evolution on the solar surface. The authors aim to analyze the photospheric physical condition changes during a specific collapse event and the resulting atmospheric response, leveraging high-resolution observations and simulations.
AI.method: The study contrasts a high-resolution radiative magneto-hydrodynamic simulation of a granular collapse performed with the CO5BOLD code against recent integral field unit spectropolarimetric observations obtained with the MiHI instrument at the Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope. Synthetic and observed Na i D1 line profiles are compared, and acoustic energy flux is estimated.
AI.result: The observed and simulated granular collapse show remarkable similarity, both exhibiting the signature of a wave pulse excited in the deep photosphere and visible up to the temperature minimum. The wave is detectable through a blue-wing emission in both observed and synthetic Na i D1 lines. The acoustic energy flux carried by the wave was estimated and its initiation analyzed.
AI.conclusion: Combining high-resolution IFU spectropolarimetry with state-of-the-art simulations of the solar lower atmosphere demonstrates current capabilities in identifying specific physical processes during granular collapse and their impact on the overlying atmosphere.

title: V557 Mon: Hot water vapour observed on an eruptive young star
summary: In this paper, we present observations of an eruptive young star in the Rosette Nebula, identified by the Gaia Science Alerts system using Gaia time series data. We aim to investigate the evolution of the brightness and mass accretion rate of V557 Mon throughout its outburst and subsequent decline. In addition, we trace the evolution of the inner accretion disk during the outburst by monitoring molecular emission features. We compiled multi-band photometric time series from Gaia, ZTF, and several 1 m-class ground-based telescopes and obtained optical and near-infrared spectra at multiple epochs covering the outburst and fading phases. Stellar parameters were derived from quiescent colour/spectra and spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. We also measured the mass accretion rate and fit models to molecular emission bands. Since late 2024, V557 Mon has undergone a year-long outburst consistent with EXor variability. Based on quiescent photometry, V557~Mon has a spectral type of M1 with an extinction of AV = 1.8+_0.3 mag, consistent with a 0.4-0.5 M_sol star at an age of 2 Myr. Our multi-epoch spectra and u-band photometry indicate a peak accretion rate of 6.3x10^(-7)M_sol/yr during the outburst, roughly 70 times higher than in quiescence. We report the detection of hot water vapour emission bands, together with TiO, VO, and CO emission features. Using ExoMol models, we measured the inner-disk temperature changed from 3000 K to 2000 K during the fading phase of the outburst. We report a recent EXor outburst in a low-mass Class II YSO. Our observations reveal the transient formation of a hot molecular inner disk, traced by variable water vapour emission during the EXor event. A positive correlation is found between the molecular excitation temperature and the overall stellar brightness.

AI.tldr: V557 Mon, a low-mass Class II young stellar object in the Rosette Nebula identified by Gaia Science Alerts, underwent a year-long EXor-type outburst since late 2024. Multi-band photometry and spectra reveal a peak accretion rate of 6.3×10⁻⁷ M_sun/yr (70× quiescence) and transient hot water vapour, TiO, VO, and CO emission from an inner disk whose temperature dropped from 3000 K to 2000 K during fading, with a positive correlation between molecular excitation temperature and stellar brightness.
AI.motivation: To investigate the evolution of brightness and mass accretion rate of V557 Mon throughout its EXor outburst and subsequent decline, and to trace the evolution of the inner accretion disk via molecular emission features during the eruptive event.
AI.method: Compiled multi-band photometric time series from Gaia, ZTF, and 1 m-class ground-based telescopes; obtained multi-epoch optical and near-infrared spectra covering outburst and fading phases; derived stellar parameters from quiescent colours/spectra and SED fitting; measured mass accretion rate and fit ExoMol models to molecular emission bands.
AI.result: V557 Mon is an M1 spectral type star with AV=1.8±0.3 mag, consistent with a 0.4–0.5 M_sun star at ~2 Myr. Peak accretion rate reached 6.3×10⁻⁷ M_sun/yr during outburst (~70× quiescence). Detected hot water vapour, TiO, VO, and CO emission; inner-disk temperature decreased from 3000 K to 2000 K during fading. A positive correlation exists between molecular excitation temperature and stellar brightness.
AI.conclusion: V557 Mon represents a recently identified EXor outburst in a low-mass Class II YSO, revealing transient formation of a hot molecular inner disk traced by variable water vapour emission, with molecular excitation temperature positively correlated to overall stellar brightness.

title: Statistical Study of Solar Prominence Plumes Based on NVST H$α$ Observations
comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Plumes are one of the most representative dynamic features observed in prominences and play a key role in mass and magnetic transport within them. However, their physical nature and triggering processes remain actively debated. Based on limb H$α$ observations from the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) during 2013--2025, we statistically investigated 34 plumes with clear and complete evolutions by developing an automated image-processing pipeline. It is revealed that plume lifetimes mainly range from 300 s to 700 s, with vertical displacements between 3--7 Mm. The mean widths and velocities are concentrated in the range of 0.5--1.5 Mm and 10--20 km s$^{-1}$, respectively. Besides wide distribution ranges, plume parameters exhibit irregular evolution fluctuations, indicating that the formation and evolution of various plumes may exhibit different physical patterns. Correlation analysis among the parameters further reveals that: (1) Positive correlations were found among lifetime, vertical displacement, and mean width, indicating an intrinsic coupling between the temporal and spatial scales of plumes. (2) Trajectory curvature is negatively correlated with lifetime, vertical displacement, and velocity. Accelerating and width-contracting plumes typically have lower curvature, suggesting that curvature may reflect environmental influences and the stability of plumes. (3) Plumes with higher initial velocities were more likely to be accompanied by precursor brightening, suggesting that these plumes may be triggered by magnetic reconnection. Furthermore, we infer that some plumes in non-bubble regions may be inherently driven by mini-filament eruptions. These results establish a statistical framework for prominence plumes and reveal diversity in their dynamical evolution and triggering mechanisms.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a statistical study of 34 solar prominence plumes observed by the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) from 2013–2025. Using an automated image-processing pipeline, the authors characterize plume lifetimes (300–700 s), vertical displacements (3–7 Mm), widths (0.5–1.5 Mm), and velocities (10–20 km/s), revealing irregular evolutionary fluctuations. Correlation analyses show intrinsic coupling between temporal and spatial scales, curvature negatively correlates with lifetime/displacement/velocity, and higher initial velocities are associated with precursor brightening—suggesting magnetic reconnection triggers—while some non-bubble region plumes may be driven by mini-filament eruptions.
AI.motivation: Plumes are prominent dynamic features in solar prominences that play key roles in mass and magnetic transport, yet their physical nature and triggering processes remain actively debated. This work aims to establish a comprehensive statistical framework to characterize plume parameters and uncover their triggering mechanisms.
AI.method: The authors developed an automated image-processing pipeline and statistically analyzed 34 plumes with clear, complete evolutions using limb Hα observations from NVST spanning 2013–2025. Parameter measurements and correlation analyses were performed across multiple physical quantities including lifetime, vertical displacement, width, velocity, and trajectory curvature.
AI.result: Plume lifetimes mainly range 300–700 s with vertical displacements of 3–7 Mm, mean widths of 0.5–1.5 Mm, and velocities of 10–20 km/s. Positive correlations exist among lifetime, vertical displacement, and width. Trajectory curvature is negatively correlated with lifetime, displacement, and velocity. Plumes with higher initial velocities are more likely accompanied by precursor brightening, suggesting magnetic reconnection as a trigger.
AI.conclusion: The results establish a statistical framework for prominence plumes and reveal diversity in their dynamical evolution and triggering mechanisms. Plume parameters exhibit irregular fluctuations indicating different physical patterns, and some non-bubble region plumes may be inherently driven by mini-filament eruptions rather than other mechanisms.

title: Horizontal Magnetic Fields Dominate the Quiet Sun Internetwork in Sunrise III Observations. Evidence from Traditional and Transformer-Based Inversions
summary: The relative prevalence of horizontal and vertical magnetic fields in the quiet-Sun internetwork remains debated, owing to the weak linear polarisation signals that make the inferred magnetic inclination distributions sensitive to observational quality and inversion methodology. We investigate the magnetic topology of the quiet-Sun internetwork in {\sc Sunrise~iii} observations by independently applying transformer-based and traditional inversion techniques to the same spectropolarimetric dataset. We analyse observations obtained with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter (SCIP). Transformer-based inversions (SINN), trained exclusively on synthetic Stokes profiles generated from a large radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulation, are compared with independent inversions performed using the \textsc{DeSIRe} code. Both inversion methods recover a quiet-Sun magnetic topology in which internetwork fields are strongly dominated by the horizontal component, whereas network fields exhibit a substantially more balanced topology. At $\logτ=-1.2$, the median horizontal and unsigned line-of-sight field components in the internetwork are 64 and 7G with \textsc{DeSIRe}, and 71 and 8G with SINN, respectively, corresponding to a horizontal-to-line-of-sight ratio of approximately nine for both methods. The agreement between the two fundamentally different inversion methodologies indicates that the quiet-Sun internetwork is characterised by a substantially stronger horizontal than vertical magnetic field component. These results demonstrate that transformer-based inversions can be successfully transferred from synthetic training data to real spectropolarimetric observations, while providing inference orders of magnitude faster than traditional inversion techniques.

AI.tldr: The paper compares transformer-based (SINN) and traditional (DeSIRe) inversion techniques on the same Sunrise III/SCIP spectropolarimetric dataset to determine the magnetic topology of the quiet-Sun internetwork. Both methods independently confirm that internetwork fields are strongly dominated by horizontal components (with a horizontal-to-line-of-sight ratio of ~9), while network fields are more balanced. The transformer inversion is orders of magnitude faster and transfers successfully from synthetic to real data.
AI.motivation: The relative prevalence of horizontal versus vertical magnetic fields in the quiet-Sun internetwork is debated, because weak linear polarisation signals make inferred magnetic inclination distributions sensitive to observational quality and inversion methodology.
AI.method: Two independent inversion approaches are applied to the same Sunrise III spectropolarimetric dataset from SCIP: (1) a transformer-based inversion (SINN) trained exclusively on synthetic Stokes profiles from a large radiative MHD simulation, and (2) the traditional DeSIRe inversion code. The resulting magnetic field topologies are compared.
AI.result: Both methods recover a topology where internetwork fields are strongly horizontal-dominated, whereas network fields are more balanced. At logτ=-1.2, median horizontal and unsigned LOS fields in the internetwork are 64/7 G (DeSIRe) and 71/8 G (SINN), giving a horizontal-to-LOS ratio of about nine for both methods.
AI.conclusion: The agreement between two fundamentally different inversion methodologies indicates that the quiet-Sun internetwork is characterised by a substantially stronger horizontal than vertical magnetic field component. Transformer-based inversions transfer successfully from synthetic training to real data and provide orders-of-magnitude faster inference than traditional techniques.

title: Expanding magnetic canopy structure and parasitic polarities in a quiet-Sun network element observed by Sunrise III/SCIP
summary: We present high-resolution multi-line spectropolarimetric observations of a quiet-Sun network element obtained with the {\sc Sunrise~iii} Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter. The observations combine photospheric, upper-photospheric, and chromospheric diagnostics at a spatial resolution and polarimetric sensitivity that allow the transverse magnetic structure of the network boundary to be examined directly. We find that the strongest linear polarisation is concentrated in a narrow ridge around the edge of the magnetic element, co-spatial with enhanced transverse magnetic field inferred from multiline inversions. The magnetic azimuth exhibits a coherent, predominantly radial organisation around a more vertical core, consistent with an expanding magnetic canopy. An azimuth proxy derived directly from the observed Fe~\textsc{i} and K~\textsc{i} linear polarisation reproduces the same large-scale organisation, showing that this structure is encoded in the Stokes profiles rather than imposed by the inversion. Response functions and a MURaM-based forward-synthesis test indicate that the Fe~\textsc{i}~8468~Å linear polarisation is sensitive to magnetic azimuth in the upper photosphere, with the closest proxy agreement occurring near $\logτ\approx-3$. We find no evidence for strong azimuthal shear between the Fe- and K-sensitive diagnostics. At the network boundary, we also identify localised parasitic-polarity patches associated with complex, multi-lobed Stokes $V$ profiles, and one case in which the Stokes $V$ polarity reverses between photospheric Fe~\textsc{i} and chromospheric Ca~\textsc{ii} lines. These results demonstrate that quiet-Sun network boundaries contain organised upper-photospheric canopy fields together with small-scale mixed-polarity structure, providing new constraints on the three-dimensional magnetic structure of network elements.

AI.tldr: Using high-resolution multi-line spectropolarimetric observations from Sunrise III's Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter, the study reveals that quiet-Sun network elements exhibit a narrow ridge of strong linear polarization at their boundary with a coherent, radially organized transverse magnetic field forming an expanding canopy. Fe I 8468 Å polarization traces azimuth in the upper photosphere (log τ ≈ -3), and local parasitic-polarity patches with complex Stokes V profiles are found, including one polarity reversal between photospheric and chromospheric lines.
AI.motivation: To directly examine the transverse magnetic structure of quiet-Sun network boundaries, which has been difficult to observe at sufficient spatial resolution and polarimetric sensitivity, and to constrain the three-dimensional magnetic topology of network elements in the upper photosphere and chromosphere.
AI.method: High-resolution multi-line spectropolarimetric observations combining photospheric (Fe I), upper-photospheric, and chromospheric (K I, Ca II) diagnostics; multiline inversions to infer magnetic field; magnetic azimuth proxy derived directly from observed Stokes profiles; response functions and MURaM-based forward-synthesis tests to validate azimuth sensitivity.
AI.result: Strongest linear polarization forms a narrow ridge at the network boundary co-spatial with enhanced transverse field. Magnetic azimuth shows coherent, radial organization around a more vertical core (expanding canopy). The azimuth proxy from observed Stokes profiles reproduces this organization, confirming the structure is inherent in the data. Fe I 8468 Å responds to azimuth near log τ ≈ -3 with no strong azimuthal shear between Fe and K diagnostics. Localized parasitic-polarity patches show multi-lobed Stokes V, including one photospheric-chromospheric polarity reversal.
AI.conclusion: Quiet-sun network boundaries contain organized upper-photospheric canopy fields coexisting with small-scale mixed-polarity structures, providing new observational constraints on the three-dimensional magnetic structure of network elements.
